test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 31 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A sum of ₹100 was invested for two years at 10% compound interest per annum. If the rate of interest is increased to 20% for the same period, how much more will the investor get as interest?
solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹100

Rate of interest (r1) = 10% per annum

Rate of interest (r2) = 20% per annum

Time (t) = 2 years

**Formula used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)t

Where, A = Amount after time t

**Calculations:**

For r1 = 10%:

A1 = 100(1 + 10/100)²

⇒ A1 = 100(1 + 0.1)²

⇒ A1 = 100(1.1)²

⇒ A1 = 100 × 1.21

⇒ A1 = ₹121

For r2 = 20%:

A2 = 100(1 + 20/100)²

⇒ A2 = 100(1 + 0.2)²

⇒ A2 = 100(1.2)²

⇒ A2 = 100 × 1.44

⇒ A2 = ₹144

Extra interest earned:

Extra interest = A2 - A1

⇒ Extra interest = 144 - 121

⇒ Extra interest = ₹23

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**
